items.title: Elvin Jones — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: it was J.R Montrose, Teddy Charles and Mingus and myself. So that’s that quartet

ctx.x: So you remained in New York after the auditions. You met Kenny Clarke and Philly Joe and you were still in New York and that’s when you got a call from Mingus and this was about a week’s span, a day’s span?

Yeah the next day (after the audition) I got a call from Mingus. First Miles called me and he wanted me to go out with him and I said, “No man, play with Joe. What are you talking about are you going to go out with two drummers?” And then the sort of Sauter- Finegan (Orchestra)’s manager called me to do a rehearsal with the Sauter Finegan band. And I had to pass on that one. And then Mingus called me and he said, “We’re going out” and it was J.R Montrose, Teddy Charles and Mingus and myself. So that’s that…
So you’re getting these calls. Was it cause of Hank’s connections or did you have a reputation already in New York?
